comments.text: IT Guy here, PSA DO NOT UPDATE your printers firmware, it is a blacklist for generic ink carts. Also if you do get blacklisted contact your ink supplier and see if they have a refund policy, or can send out a different set. Sometimes they can walk you though a firmware downgrade to get them working again. Most of the time they know they are playing a cat a mouse game with the printer companies. Better yet, get a laser if you don't print that often, or an ink jet tank system like the Mega Tanks or Eco tanks for ink, saves a lot and removed most of the DRM that cartridges come with. You absolutely do NOT have to sign up for a subscription service those are all OPTIONAL on every printer, HP is the most egregious about it with weird dark patterns built in to trick you into signing up. They can be alright for you but are hard to unenroll from once it's started. If you had ink and you enroll in these plans, your tossing the ink and buying genuine carts for at least your first time out of the gate if you do drop the subscription, it will Locke them down even if there is ink in there... All printers are disposable, so treat it was such, and grab a cheep one that meets your needs. Also just avoid HP in general they suck these days. Peace out peeps!

IT'S THE HP SOFTWARE.
It's running on the computer and communicating over the internet.  Using the software with one of the target printer will result in the printer being flagged and you'll then be "encouraged" to connect the printer to network . . .

That said, when/while using the HP app, some individuals inadvertently activate HP+ and or the HP subscription service.
HP+ offers extended warranty for a device and allows one to use web and cell phone integration; but it forces the use of HP ink forever.  The subscription service is a different plan that does allow one to opt out (*** after satisfying the minimum subscription period/requirements ***).

So, when you get an HP message on your screen, try to slow down and read it; hastily clicking "OK" might make it go away but it might come back to haunt you.
